userStories.title: Create known-athletes-2026.json with Julia and Lilah Versluis
userStories.description:
Current state: config/known-athletes-2025.json exists with 25 Triple Jump athletes. No 2026 config exists.

What to build: Create businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/config/known-athletes-2026.json that:
  1. Copies all 25 athletes from known-athletes-2025.json, setting 'year_2026' from their 'year_2026_expected' field, keeping all other fields
  2. Adds Julia Versluis: {"name": "Julia Versluis", "school": "Georgia Southern", "school_slug": "georgia-southern", "year_2025": "SO-2", "year_2026": "JR-3", "events": ["Triple Jump", "High Jump"], "tfrrs_id": "8695140"}
  3. Adds Lilah Versluis: {"name": "Lilah Versluis", "school": "South Florida", "school_slug": "south-florida", "year_2025": "FR-1", "year_2026": "SO-2", "events": ["High Jump", "Triple Jump", "Long Jump"], "tfrrs_id": "9272064"}

Constraints:
- File must be valid JSON array
- Do NOT remove any of the 25 existing athletes
- Use 'events' (array) instead of 'event' (string) for all entries — this is the 2026 schema change
- Julia and Lilah tfrrs_ids are verified correct — do not change them
acceptance: python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/config/known-athletes-2026.json')); ids=[a['tfrrs_id'] for a in d]; assert '8695140' in ids,'Julia missing'; assert '9272064' in ids,'Lilah missing'; assert len(d)>=27,'expected 27+ athletes, got '+str(len(d)); print('PASS -',len(d),'athletes')"
python3 -m json.tool businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/config/known-athletes-2026.json > /dev/null && echo VALID_JSON || echo INVALID_JSON

userStories.title: seed_known_athletes.py — upsert known athletes into DB
userStories.description:
Current state: known-athletes-2026.json exists (after US-TF002). DB has 137 athletes but Julia (tfrrs_id 8695140) is MISSING entirely, and Lilah (tfrrs_id 9272064) has 14 performances but NO athlete record (orphaned). predict_event.py queries the athletes table — missing athlete records means Julia/Lilah never appear in predictions.

What to build: Create businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/seed_known_athletes.py that:
  1. Reads config/known-athletes-2026.json (path relative to script: ../config/known-athletes-2026.json)
  2. For each athlete, calls db.upsert_athlete({tfrrs_id, name, school_slug, year, events_list_as_json_string})
  3. Prints a summary: 'Seeded N athletes. NEW: X, UPDATED: Y'
  4. Adds sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent)) so sibling db.py import works

DB path note: import db (sibling script). db.py uses Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] as REPO_ROOT → resolves to businesses/ → DB at businesses/data/tf-predictor/tf-predictor.db.

Constraints:
- Do NOT delete or modify existing athlete records not in known-athletes-2026.json
- Script must be runnable from workspace root: python3 businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/seed_known_athletes.py
- Must be idempotent (safe to re-run)
- Check db.upsert_athlete() signature in db.py before writing the call
acceptance: python3 businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/seed_known_athletes.py 2>&1 | grep -q 'Seeded' && echo PASS || echo FAIL

userStories.title: run_pipeline.sh — end-to-end prediction orchestration script
userStories.description:
Current state: All individual scripts exist (scrape_meet_entries.py, scrape_athlete_marks.py, predict_event.py, generate_report.py) but there is no orchestration wrapper. Predictions must be run manually step by step.

What to build: Create businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/run_pipeline.sh that:
  1. Accepts args: --meet-id <slug> --tfrrs-url <url> --events <comma-list> --year <year> [--skip-scrape]
  2. Step 1: scrape meet entries — python3 scripts/scrape_meet_entries.py --url $TFRRS_URL --meet-id $MEET_ID --events $EVENTS
  3. Step 2 (unless --skip-scrape): for each athlete in the entries output, scrape marks — python3 scripts/scrape_athlete_marks.py --input businesses/data/tf-predictor/meets/$MEET_ID/entries/{first_event}-f_all.json --events "$EVENTS_HUMAN"
  4. Step 3: for each event slug, run predict — python3 scripts/predict_event.py --event $EVENT --meet $MEET_ID --year $YEAR
  5. Step 4: generate report — python3 scripts/generate_report.py --meet $MEET_ID --year $YEAR
  6. Print PIPELINE_COMPLETE at the end

Event slug mapping (add to script as a lookup): triple-jump, long-jump, high-jump → 'Triple Jump', 'Long Jump', 'High Jump'
All python3 calls must be run from the tf-predictor directory (the script cds there at the start).
Add --dry-run flag that prints the steps without executing them.

Constraints:
- All paths inside the shell script are relative to tf-predictor/ directory
- Must be executable: chmod +x
- Must handle errors (set -e)
- --help flag prints usage
acceptance: bash businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/run_pipeline.sh --help 2>&1 | grep -qi 'usage\|meet-id' && echo PASS || echo FAIL

bash businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/run_pipeline.sh --meet-id test-meet --tfrrs-url https://example.com --events triple-jump --year 2026 --dry-run 2>&1 | grep -q 'scrape_meet_entries\|DRY' && echo PASS || echo FAIL
python3 -c "import os; info=os.stat('businesses/data-services/tf-predictor/scripts/run_pipeline.sh'); print('EXECUTABLE' if info.st_mode & 0o111 else 'NOT_EXECUTABLE')"
